head_commit.message:
ci: make the real-ZFS gate prove what it measured

check-skips.sh now fails when an allowed (simulator-only) skip did not
skip, when a listed top-level test neither passed nor skipped, when
Ginkgo ran fewer than 44 csi-sanity specs, and on any FAIL or panic
line; result lines are matched unanchored, and an entry covers its
subtests. Each was proven against crafted logs.

The VM leg drops internal/server and internal/zfs, which never touch a
pool; waits for cloud-init's boot-finished marker instead of
status --wait (ssh 255 on sshd restart); requires userland and kmod to
be the same version; prechecks the NFS prerequisites; bounds each test
binary at 8m. The workflow fails fast without /dev/kvm, uploads logs
when a timeout cancels the job, and gives each push to main its own
concurrency group.

head_commit.message:
Reject zfs get output that repeats a (dataset, property) line

zfs get -Hp prints user property values raw, so a value containing a
newline can forge lines for another dataset, e.g. marking a foreign
dataset as managed and committed so DeleteVolume would destroy it.
zfs prints exactly one line per (dataset, property), so a forged line
for a real dataset always collides with its genuine one: fail the scan.

head_commit.message:
Run real-ZFS contract tests on Ubuntu 26.10 (OpenZFS 2.4.4) under KVM

TrueNAS 27 RC targets OpenZFS 2.4; the hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner only has
zfs-2.2.2 userland over a 2.3.4 module. Ubuntu 26.10 (stonking) ships
zfs-linux 2.4.4-1ubuntu4, but GitHub has no runner for it and ZFS lives in
the kernel, so a container would still test the host's ZFS.

ci/real-zfs-vm.sh boots the 26.10 cloud image under KVM on the hosted
runner, installs zfsutils-linux via cloud-init, copies in statically built
test binaries and runs the same contract tests against a file-backed pool.
The 24.04 host job stays as real-zfs-noble for older-ZFS compatibility.

head_commit.message:
Fix second adversarial review findings; create filesystems unshared

- an exported pool reads as 'dataset does not exist': a missing volume is
  only absent when its parent exists, else Unavailable (DeleteSnapshot
  no longer reports OK on a dead pool)
- pool-root parents: the parent's own snapshots are not volume rows
- snapshot ids that cannot fit 128 bytes are rejected, not returned
- a zfs binary that never ran is reported as such, not 'exit -1'
- daemon: refuse to unlink a live socket (a second daemon would bring its
  own lock table); create the socket 0600 under umask in a 0700 dir;
  bounded drain on shutdown, second signal stops at once
- filesystems and their clones are created with sharenfs/sharesmb=off:
  both inherit, so a shared parent would export every new volume to '*'

docs/research/gaps: designs for file export, block export, fencing and
the CSI front end, each with its adversarial reviews.

head_commit.message:
Accept any CSI snapshot name up to 128 bytes

Snapshot ids were '<volume>@<name>', so a 128-byte name (which csi-sanity
creates and expects to succeed) produced an id over CSI's 128-byte limit
and was rejected; names valid in CSI but not in zfs were rejected too.

The zfs snapshot component is now the CSI name when it is a valid zfs
name and the id fits, else 'csi-' + a stable hash of it. The CSI name is
kept in csi_snapshot_name, which lookups already match on, so retries
stay idempotent.

head_commit.message:
Classify property ENOSPC errors; size the CI pool for thick zvols

First run on real ZFS (OpenZFS 2.3.4): 15 of 18 contract tests passed
unchanged. The 3 failures were the 2G test pool running out of space for
thick zvols, which exposed a real gap: 'size is greater than available
space' (zfs_setprop_error, libzfs_util.c) was unclassified and surfaced
as Internal instead of ResourceExhausted, so CSI sidecars would treat a
full pool as a non-retryable bug.

- classify both zfs_setprop_error ENOSPC texts (reservation: no space;
  quota below used: invalid property)
- CI pool is a 20G sparse file (thick zvols reserve, the file stays empty)
- push trigger back to main only: the PR's pull_request event covers the
  branch, so every push no longer runs CI twice

head_commit.message:
Raise simulator fidelity to audited OpenZFS behavior; run CI on all branches

Three audits of zfstest.Sim against OpenZFS source (cmd/zfs, libzfs,
zfs_prop.c, the cli_root test suites) found divergences that could hide
endpoint bugs. Fixed the ones the endpoint can reach:

- create -V rounds up to volblocksize; -s without -V errors; volsize 0
  rejected; refreservation=auto resolves, volumes only; missing pool
  reports 'no such pool'
- clones copy volblocksize; snapshot -o accepts user properties only
- destroy -d on a filesystem errors; missing snapshots use the real text
- get: type-inapplicable properties print '-'; unknown property names
  error; snapshot depth counts from the snapshot's own dataset
- inherit refuses quota/reservation/volsize; compression default is on

CI now runs on pushes to every branch: the repository has no default
branch, and the real-ZFS job is the oracle the simulator answers to.
